Kimberly / team,

I've reviewed the attachments quickly and pulled out immediate redline positions for discussion:

1) VPC hosting carveout — we can accept a narrowly scoped carveout limited to specific data types listed in an exhibit (e.g., PII tagged as "sensitive" for EU patients). We should avoid broad language that implies dedicated infrastructure. Proposed language: allow Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) as an option where required by law or contract but tie to a 90-day implementation lead time and an SOW for infra costs.

2) SCCs mapping — some of their proposed transfer flows are fine but the mapping currently assumes we act as controller for certain enrichment workflows. We should keep the controller/processor split consistent with our standard DPA. I will annotate the SCCs_Mapping sheet with row-level comments (attachment).

3) Subprocessor objection window — 10 business days is short for enterprise legal review. Recommend 15 business days with an interim mitigation process (we continue processing under existing terms unless ZenithCare invokes specific suspension rights).

4) Order Form version pinning — acceptable if we carve out model upgrades that may affect cost/latency and add a clause allowing Redwood to propose model variant upgrades with customer opt-out within 30 days. Ben: any billing/pricing flags?

I'll prepare a tracked-change DPA draft and a summary memo for the call.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (in thread) ZenithCare_Redline_DPA_v3.docx — annotated; SCCs_Mapping_ZenithCare.xlsx — comments added

Quick run from commercial/finance POV:

- Version pinning on the Order Form: OK if we include a pricing reopener tied to material feature changes. We should specify that security patches and minor model parameter tuning do not trigger re-pricing.
- VPC carveout: expect an implementation SOW and a one-time provisioning fee plus a run-rate uplift. I'll draft a short pricing note (estimate) for Laura to attach to the DPA memo.
- Objection window: 15 business days seems reasonable from a procurement cycle perspective. If they insist on 10, we can accept for customers with enterprise contracts but put in an exec-level approval path and financial buffer clause.

I'll be on the Wed 10–11 PT window for the redline review.

Ben Carter
